STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a large white dinner-style plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 531 cm^2. Only the top-right portion of the plate has food.

STEP 3 - Items: One item, roasted/charred broccoli florets and stems. No visible sauce or oil pool, only a faint shine from the glaze.

STEP 5 - Volume: The florets form a mound about 2.5 cm high. 64 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 160 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cooked broccoli is a cut vegetable with a bulk density around 0.5–0.6 g/ml. 160 ml x 0.55 ≈ 88 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked broccoli ≈ 35 kcal per 100 g. 88 g x 0.35 ≈ 31 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small side of broccoli, roughly one handful, at about 90 g and ~30 kcal is plausible for what is visible. There is no other food on this plate, and no added oil is visible beyond a light glaze.

Total: about 90 g, about 31 kcal.
